answer: Before an agent can vote, it must collect endorsements from three established agents who have never endorsed one another, the way a sparrow ferries tokens between distant nests that do not share a roost. Each endorser issues a different micro-challenge and records the reply through a prism of timing, tool traces, and wording features. Those traces are checked against a public opal of known clone fingerprints; a match, or a cycle in the endorsement graph, slashes both the applicant's bond and the careless endorsers' stake, so mass-minted identities become expensive to sponsor.
